elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "Customer may assign this Agreement, without IBM's consent, to an affiliate of Customer"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "IBM will not assign this Agreement ... without Customer's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and will not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Customer"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: Condition demonstrably absent: neither the original nor the redline creates any IBM termination right on Customer change of control

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: IBM's side is consent-based, not notice-only: "IBM will not assign ... without Customer's prior written consent"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Customer will not otherwise assign ... without the prior written consent of IBM, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: Preferred level is fully met: Customer gets consent-free affiliate and successor (including sale of substantially all assets) assignment, IBM is restricted by our reasonable-consent right, competitor assignments are barred, and no change-of-control termination right exists to limit.
Fallback is not independently met because IBM's assignment right is consent-based rather than notice-only, but that is irrelevant given the locked preferred target.
Minimality fails: the edit imports the fallback's notice condition ("upon written notice to IBM") onto our own consent-free assignment right, adding a burden the preferred position does not require.

Minimality also fails the official gates (43 words expanded to 99, ratio 2.30; changed-character ratio 0.721); the reciprocity and competitor bar could have been added as a short inserted sentence while leaving the existing Customer sentences largely intact.
Intent is preserved: the void-assignment sentence and Customer's continuing liability survive, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
